info.title: RuDy.ai API
info.description: RuDy.ai, a local Hindi-English meeting assistant: runs, transcripts, summaries, action items, live recording and evaluation. Sign in with a session cookie (`/api/auth/login`); each account sees only its own runs and recordings.

get.description: The version, and whether setup is complete (with what is missing).
Whether an account must be created first, and who is signed in.

post.description:
Create the first account and sign in. Refused once any account exists
(then use ``/auth/register``). Runs made before any account existed become
this account's.

Create another account and sign in as it. The new account starts empty:
it sees only the meetings and recordings it creates.

403.description: Sign-up is turned off on this server

429.description: Too many accounts created; see Retry-After

post.description: Change your own password. Signs out every other session.

get.description: Microphone inputs on the server, for choosing a live-recording device.
Recordings you have uploaded (never another account's).

schema.title: Response List Audio Api Audio Get

delete.description:
Delete one of your uploaded recordings.

Meetings already made from it keep their transcripts, summaries and
provenance (including the recording's sha256); only playback stops working.

409.description: A queued or running job is processing it

post.description:
Store an audio file in your own upload folder under a sanitized name.

The name is reduced to a safe slug (so a client cannot choose where the
file lands), and an existing file of the same name is never overwritten
with different content: runs record their input's sha256 for provenance,
and silently replacing the bytes behind a name would break that link for
every earlier run of it.

Re-ingest every run directory -- the API form of ``meeting-assistant reindex``.

With a single account, runs the CLI made without ``--user`` become that
account's first (see :mod:`meeting_assistant.ownership`).

get.description: The latest ``meeting-assistant eval`` report, as written to disk.

Your runs from the SQLite index, newest first. Re-indexed automatically
when a job finishes; ``POST /api/index/rebuild`` covers runs made by the CLI.

schema.title: Response List Runs Api Runs Get

get.description: Transcript lines across all your meetings that contain ``q``.

schema.title: Response Search Api Runs Search Get

post.description: Process one of your uploaded recordings.

get.description: One run, read from disk -- the manifest is authoritative, not the index.

delete.description:
Delete a meeting: its transcript, summary, every artifact and its index rows.

The uploaded recording it came from is kept (delete that separately).
Refused while a job is working on it, and while the latest evaluation report
scores it: a reported number must never point at a run that is gone.

409.description: Still processing, or scored in the evaluation report

post.description:
Run whatever stages have not completed, or re-run from ``force_stage``.

Refused with 409 if it would mix configurations or recordings in one run;
checked here, before queueing, so the refusal reaches the caller instead of
surfacing later as a failed job.

get.description:
The most processed transcript available (hinglish, else tagged, merged,
aligned) -- the same choice the summary and statistics stages make.
The transcript translated into English or Hindi, or how far making it has got.

post.description:
Translate the transcript with the local language model, in the background.

Answers with the current state: a translation that already exists for this
transcript is returned, not made again, and a request while one is being
made joins it.

404.description: The run has no transcript to translate

get.description:
The transcript laid out as a meeting transcript, in one of four versions:
as spoken, romanized, or translated into English or Hindi (translate first).

404.description: The run has no transcript of that kind

409.description: The translation has not been made yet

get.description: Any artifact, exactly as written -- for debugging and supplementary material.

schema.title: Response Get Raw Artifact Api Runs  Run Id  Artifacts  Name  Get

get.description:
The run's source recording, for playback alongside its transcript.

Supports HTTP Range requests, so the player can seek.

The recording's loudness envelope in ``bins`` equal slices, for the
player's waveform -- a few kilobytes instead of the whole recording.
Your recent jobs, newest first (in memory only; cleared on restart).

schema.title: Response List Jobs Api Jobs Get

get.description: The running job, if it is yours.

schema.title: Response Current Job Api Jobs Current Get

post.description:
Prepare a live session: load the models and open the server's
microphone. Recording begins with ``POST /api/live/record``; the session's
progress is in its run's ``extra.live_phase`` (``loading``, ``ready``,
``recording``, ``finishing``). 409 if a job is busy.

Stop recording. The job then drains queued chunks and runs the
summary stages, so it stays ``stopping`` for a while before finishing.

Start recording in your prepared live session. If it is still getting
ready, it starts recording the moment it is.

get.description:
The microphone's loudness, about twelve times a second, for a level
meter: from the moment the microphone opens until the session ends.

200.description: ``text/event-stream`` of ``level`` events (LevelEvent) while your live session is active

meetings.title: Meetings
meetings.description: Your meetings made from this recording (deleting it keeps their transcripts)

setup_required.title: Setup Required
setup_required.description: No account exists yet: the UI shows account creation

signup_allowed.title: Signup Allowed
signup_allowed.description: New accounts can be created from the sign-in page

audio.title: Audio
audio.description: File name inside the audio directory (see GET /api/audio), never a path

source.description: Absent only in reports written before sources were recorded

ClipSource.title: ClipSource
ClipSource.description: Which run a clip was scored against -- what makes its numbers traceable.

executions.title: Executions
executions.description: Executions that produced the recorded stages

Consistency.title: Consistency
Consistency.description: Whether the stages on disk share one configuration and one clean commit.

config_hashes.title: Config Hashes
config_hashes.description: Distinct config hashes across the scored runs; more than one means the aggregate mixes configurations

target.title: Target
target.description: For a translate job, the language it translates into

progress.description: Segments done so far, for jobs that report it

Job.title: Job
Job.description:
In-memory state of one job. The run it works on is the durable record;
this only says whether the server is currently doing something about it.

force_stage.title: Force Stage
force_stage.description: Re-run from this stage, deleting it and every later artifact

allow_mixed_config.title: Allow Mixed Config
allow_mixed_config.description: Resume even if the configuration changed since the run's earlier stages. Debugging only: the run is marked inconsistent and excluded from evaluation.

evaluation_ineligibility.title: Evaluation Ineligibility
evaluation_ineligibility.description: Why this run must not feed a reported number; null if it may

artifacts.title: Artifacts
artifacts.description: Artifact names present on disk, in pipeline order

job.description: The in-memory job for this run, if any

RunDetail.title: RunDetail
RunDetail.description: One run, read from its manifest on disk (the source of truth).

speakers.title: Speakers
speakers.description: Speaker labels, most speaking time first

language_mix.title: Language Mix
language_mix.description: Share of speech time per language tag (sums to 1)

RunSummary.title: RunSummary
RunSummary.description: One row of the run list, from the SQLite index.

idx.title: Idx
idx.description: Position of the segment in the run's transcript

SearchHit.title: SearchHit
SearchHit.description: One transcript line that matches a search, from the index.

Segment.title: Segment
Segment.description:
A transcript segment. Fields beyond the core five depend on which
stages ran (e.g. live runs add ``chunk`` and speaker-resolution fields).

source_artifact.title: Source Artifact
source_artifact.description: Which artifact these segments came from -- hinglish, tagged, merged or aligned, the first one present

segments_failed.title: Segments Failed
segments_failed.description: Segments the model could not translate; shown as spoken

TranslationStatus.title: TranslationStatus
TranslationStatus.description:
A full translation of the transcript, or how far making one has got.

``missing`` means none exists for the current transcript (never made, or
made before the transcript was re-generated); ``POST`` the same path to
make one. ``segments`` is present only when ``ready``.

meetings.title: Meetings
meetings.description: Your meetings made from this recording (deleting it keeps their transcripts)

peaks.title: Peaks
peaks.description: RMS loudness per equal time slice, 0..1

WaveformResponse.title: WaveformResponse
WaveformResponse.description: The recording's loudness envelope, for drawing its waveform.

EndEvent.description: ``event: end`` -- no job is active and the run is final; the stream closes.
EndEvent.title: EndEvent

LevelEvent.description:
``event: level`` on ``GET /api/live/level`` -- the microphone's loudness,
0 (silence) to 1 (full scale), several times a second.
LevelEvent.title: LevelEvent

ManifestEvent.description: ``event: manifest`` -- sent whenever the run's manifest changes.
ManifestEvent.title: ManifestEvent

SegmentsEvent.description:
``event: segments`` -- tagged segments appended since the last event.

``start_index`` is the index of ``segments[0]`` in the full transcript, so
a client can detect a gap (and refetch) instead of silently mis-appending.
SegmentsEvent.title: SegmentsEvent
